messages:
mike_support: FYI ticket C-9121 — customer reports a sudden billing spike after seeing 5xx errors and long latency. They attached request IDs and say logs show hits routed to both us-west-2 and eu-central-1 for the same logical request.

jen: do we have the routing headers or request ids they shared?

mike_support: pasted their excerpt below (sanitized):

Customer excerpt:
`request_id: r-7c4a1b`
`x-routing: route=acme-failover;policy=v2`
`trace: region=us-west-2 then eu-central-1`

sre-bot: ALERT: failover policy change detected for org acme at 2026-03-08T11:59:12Z — change id ch-221.

sre-bot: config snapshot: ```{
  "org": "acme",
  "failover": [
    {"region":"us-west-2","priority":1,"weight":0.7},
    {"region":"eu-central-1","priority":2,"weight":0.3}
  ],
  "sticky": true
}```

eng-liam: I think I see the root: they flipped priority and also left sticky=true with fractional weights. Our routing code expects integer weights when sticky is enabled (legacy constraint), mixed decimals can cause non-deterministic selection + fallback loops when the chosen replica fails mid-stream. That can create retries that land in a second region while the client retries, and we count tokens each time — explains billing spike.

jen: I reproduced locally by applying the same policy. Repro steps:
```bash
# set policy (simulated)
curl -X POST https://admin.example/policy -d @policy.json 
# then run repeated requests with a short retry window
for i in {1..5}; do
  curl -s -H "X-Client-Trace: repro-123" https://api.redwood.example/generate || true
done
```
I see alternating region hits in the routing debug header and 3 active invocations counted for one logical call.

billing-ops: can confirm customer was charged for the extra token usage. They saw ~2.8x the expected tokens during the 12:03-12:15 window. We need request ids list to issue a credit.

ops-rita: mitigation: 1) roll back policy ch-221 to previous snapshot; 2) disable sticky for that policy until we validate; 3) enable routing-trace header for acme org so we can follow cross-region paths. I can roll back now if we agree.

eng-liam: Agreed. I'll also push a validation check to the control-plane to reject policies where sticky=true and any weight is not an integer, and add a canary test that runs synthetic calls to ensure no cross-region switch on a single request id. Plan: patch + deploy within 2 hours.

mike_support: I'll tell the customer we have a rollback and a credit plan. Asking for the exact request ids (they gave 4 ids) and permission to issue a pro-rated credit.

jen: added a small unit/regression test to the repo. Repro script attached below (safe to run against staging):
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# repro sticky/weight interaction
for i in {1..10}; do
  curl -s -H "X-Routing-Policy: acme-v2" -H "X-Request-ID: repro-$i" \
    https://staging.api.redwood/generate || echo "fail $i"
done
```

sre-bot: RESOLVED: policy ch-221 rolled back by ops-rita at 2026-03-08T12:12:03Z. Alert cleared.

billing-ops: noted — please DM me the request ids and customer account id so we can process the credit.

eng-liam: follow-ups: add server-side enforcement to control-plane, add metric for same-request cross-region count (alert threshold > 0), and publish brief postmortem note for customers explaining non-deterministic routing during policy mismatches.

mike_support: Thanks team. I'll update the ticket and draft the customer-facing summary. :thumbsup:
